name: Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment
seoDesc: Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment: work out phototherapy threshold from the infant age and the total serum bilirubin. A free health calculator with…
summary: Give the Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator the infant age and the total serum bilirubin and it returns phototherapy threshold. That makes it useful for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator work?
sections.html:
The Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports phototherapy threshold in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the weeks of gestation, the risk factors and the show); then you type in the infant age and the total serum bilirubin (TSB).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A measured quantity, entered by default in hours. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in milligrams per deciliter. The unit chip switches it to any of the 3 supported units.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as 35 - 37 ⁶/₇ (near-term) and 38 or more (full term). The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as present and absent. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 3 options, such as phototherapy thresholds, exchange transfusion thresholds and none. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.

3 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Phototherapy threshold=(infant age − 1, risk factors, weeks of gestation)
Exchange transfusion threshold=(infant age − 1, risk factors, weeks of gestation)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.
  • A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Time, opening in hours
  • Bilirubin, opening in milligrams per deciliter

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the infant age and the total serum bilirubin — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns phototherapy threshold, derived from the infant age and the total serum bilirubin. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the infant age and the total serum bilirubin, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter infant age in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Infant age opens in hours and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Newborn hyperbilirubinemia assessment calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
